title: Advanced SQL
learner_context: I already write joins, GROUP BY and subqueries daily. I want the analytics-engineering tier: window functions and frame semantics, CTEs including recursive ones, set operations and their NULL behaviour, reading and acting on an EXPLAIN plan, index strategy, and query optimisation against real data volumes. PostgreSQL specifics welcome. Not database administration, not basic SELECT syntax.

modules.title: Window Function Frame Semantics and Partitioning
scope: ROWS BETWEEN vs RANGE BETWEEN framing

concepts.title: Ranking Function Mechanics
learning_objectives: Distinguish how ROW_NUMBER assigns sequential integers without gaps versus how RANK assigns integers with gaps for ties.
Explain the mechanism by which DENSE_RANK assigns sequential integers without gaps for ties.

concepts.title: Tie Handling Strategies
learning_objectives: Identify the specific tie-handling behavior that differentiates RANK from DENSE_RANK in ordered result sets.
Predict the output sequence for a dataset containing duplicate values when applying each ranking function.

concepts.title: NULL Value Impact
learning_objectives: Describe the impact of NULL values on the ordering and ranking produced by ROW_NUMBER, RANK, and DENSE_RANK.
Explain why NULLs are treated as the lowest or highest value depending on the sort direction.
concepts.withheld_reason: its Core Explanation is placeholder text and the lesson still contains the model's own deliberation; two repair attempts did not fix it

concepts.title: Partitioning Scope
learning_objectives: Define the role of the PARTITION BY clause in resetting the window frame for each distinct group.
Contrast the global scope of an ORDER BY without PARTITION BY against the scoped scope of PARTITION BY.

concepts.title: Partitioning
learning_objectives: Analyze how window functions behave when applied to aggregated data versus raw row data.
Explain the restriction preventing nested window functions in standard SQL.

concepts.title: Clause Ordering Rules
learning_objectives: Determine the correct placement of PARTITION BY relative to ORDER BY within the window specification.
Predict the result set structure when multiple columns are specified in the PARTITION BY clause.

concepts.title: ROWS Frame Definition
learning_objectives: Define the ROWS frame unit as a physical count of rows preceding or following the current row.
Explain how ROWS BETWEEN handles ties by treating each row as a distinct entity regardless of value.

concepts.title: RANGE Frame Definition
learning_objectives: Define the RANGE frame unit as a logical range of values based on the ORDER BY expression.
Describe how RANGE BETWEEN includes all rows with values equal to the current row's value within the specified bounds.

concepts.title: Frame Unit Differences
learning_objectives: Compare the performance implications of ROWS versus RANGE for large datasets with many ties.
Explain why RANGE is often slower due to the need to scan for equal values.

concepts.title: ROWS and Ties
learning_objectives: Explain how ROWS BETWEEN interacts with duplicate values in the ORDER BY column.
Predict the rows included in a ROWS frame when ties exist in the data.

concepts.title: RANGE and Ties
learning_objectives: Explain how RANGE BETWEEN interacts with duplicate values in the ORDER BY column.
Predict the rows included in a RANGE frame when ties exist in the data.

concepts.title: Tie Interaction
learning_objectives: Compare the output of SUM() over ROWS vs RANGE for a dataset with ties.
Identify scenarios where ROWS and RANGE produce identical results.

concepts.title: Cumulative Aggregates
learning_objectives: Define the concept of a cumulative sum using SUM() with an appropriate frame clause.
Explain how to implement a running total using ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.

concepts.title: Moving Averages
learning_objectives: Construct a moving average using AVG() with a symmetric frame (e.g., 1 PRECEDING TO 1 FOLLOWING).
Explain the difference between a cumulative average and a moving average.

concepts.title: Moving Average Edge Cases
learning_objectives: Identify edge cases where moving averages might produce misleading results due to sparse data.
Explain how to handle NULLs in moving average calculations.

concepts.title: Lag and Lead Functions
learning_objectives: Explain the purpose of LAG() and LEAD() in accessing previous and next row values.
Construct queries using LAG() and LEAD() with custom offset values.

concepts.title: Offset Handling
learning_objectives: Analyze the behavior of LAG() and LEAD() when the offset exceeds the number of available rows.
Explain the default value returned when no row exists for the specified offset.

concepts.title: Period-over-Period
learning_objectives: Apply LAG() and LEAD() to calculate period-over-period growth rates.
Explain the importance of ordering in the context of lag/lead calculations.

modules.title: Recursive CTEs and Set Operation Logic
scope: Intersection of sets: INTERSECT vs INTERSECT ALL
Difference of sets: EXCEPT vs EXCEPT ALL and NULL exclusion rules

concepts.title: Recursive CTE Mechanics
learning_objectives: Construct a recursive CTE to traverse a hierarchical employee reporting structure.
Identify the anchor member and recursive member within a given hierarchical query.

concepts.title: Termination and Duplication
learning_objectives: Diagnose infinite recursion loops caused by missing termination conditions.
Apply UNION ALL versus UNION to control duplicate row generation in recursion.

concepts.title: Depth and Path Tracking
learning_objectives: Calculate depth levels using integer counters within recursive steps.
Retrieve path strings using string concatenation in recursive members.

concepts.title: Sequence and Date Generation
learning_objectives: Implement recursive CTEs for generating sequential number series.
Generate date ranges for missing days in time-series analysis.

concepts.title: Bill of Materials Logic
learning_objectives: Model parent-child relationships in bill-of-materials structures.
Calculate cumulative costs propagating through assembly levels.

concepts.title: Graph Connectivity
learning_objectives: Write recursive queries to find connected components in graph data.
Detect cycles in directed graphs using visited path tracking.

concepts.title: INTERSET Semantics
learning_objectives: Execute INTERSECT to find exact row matches between two result sets.
Distinguish INTERSECT behavior from INNER JOIN on join keys.

concepts.title: INTERSECT ALL Logic
learning_objectives: Apply INTERSECT ALL to preserve duplicate row counts from input sets.
Calculate intersection cardinality using MIN(count) per group.

concepts.title: NULLs in Intersections
learning_objectives: Analyze NULL handling in INTERSECT comparisons.
Predict output when NULLs appear in intersecting columns.

concepts.title: EXCEPT Semantics
learning_objectives: Execute EXCEPT to identify rows present in the left set but not the right.
Verify EXCEPT behavior against LEFT ANTI JOIN patterns.

concepts.title: EXCEPT ALL Logic
learning_objectives: Apply EXCEPT ALL to preserve duplicate counts in difference calculations.
Compute net difference counts using MAX(0, count_left - count_right).

concepts.title: NULLs in Differences
learning_objectives: Evaluate NULL exclusion rules in EXCEPT operations.
Determine result set contents when NULLs exist in the right operand.
